Fix the bugs in the code so that when the [setLevel] function is called, it checks the value of the function parameter before running the code.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that each function is called at the right time and displays the correct tilemap and sprites.

validationItems.text: (level) parameter bubble is dragged into [else if] condition in [function setLevel] container.
validationItems.failureText: Check to see if the <0=0> comparison blocks in the [function setLevel] container compare the correct values.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Did you call the setLevel function with the correct parameters in the [on start] container and the [if then] conditional?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Are the correct parameter values inputted in each of the [call setLevel] blocks?


Solution: 

The parameter in the [call setLevel] block in the [on start] container should be changed to 1; the parameter in the [call setLevel] block in the [if then] conditional should be changed to 2.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the Level 2 tilemap and dialog box appears.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Level 2 tilemap and dialog box appear only once the Player sprite has earned 5 points.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that each function is called at the right time and displays the correct tilemap and sprites.

validationItems.text: parameter in [call setLevel] block in [on start] changed to 1; parameter in [call setLevel] block in [if then] conditional changed to 2.
validationItems.failureText: Check the parameters in the [call setLevel] blocks.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓Did you reorder the [call function] blocks in the [on start] container?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which function should be called first in the [on start] container?


Solution: 

The order of the [call setLevel] and [call makeSnowball] blocks in the [on start] container should be swapped.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the first snowball sprite appears on top of a wall, where the Player sprite cannot reach it.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the snowball sprite is placed after the tilemap has been created.

function setLevel (level: number) {
    if (level == 1) {
        tiles.setCurrentTilemap(tilemap`level3`)
    } else if (level == 2) {
        tiles.setCurrentTilemap(tilemap`level4`)
    }
    tiles.placeOnRandomTile(playerSprite, assets.tile`tile1`)
    game.showLongText("Level " + level, DialogLayout.Bottom)
}
sprites.onDestroyed(SpriteKind.Food, function (sprite) {
    makeSnowball()
})
function makeSnowball () {
    snowballSprite = sprites.create(img`

    tiles.placeOnRandomTile(snowballSprite, assets.tile`tile1`)
    snowballSprite.lifespan = randint(2000, 5000)
}

    music.play(music.melodyPlayable(music.baDing), music.PlaybackMode.UntilDone)

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that each function is called at the right time and displays the correct tilemap and sprites.

validationItems.text: Sequence of [call setLevel] and [call makeSnowball] blocks are swapped.
validationItems.failureText: Check the order that each function is called in.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Orange Belt! Before you create your final Orange Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn more about functions, which are chunks of code that run whenever they are called. You’ll learn how to create your own functions to simplify code and make something happen multiple times in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: Function Junction
badges.description: Create functions, with and without parameters, to make something happen in a project.

badges.title: Make Your Own Way
badges.description: Create a new function to be used in a project.

badges.title: Don't Forget To Call
badges.description: Call a user-created function in a project.

badges.title: Customize Your Own Way
badges.description: Create a new function that takes a parameter to be used in a project.

badges.title: Area Code
badges.description: Call a user-created function that takes a parameter in a project.
